title: Homogeneous polynomial approximations and preimages for adic evaluation
statement:
Let $C,R$ be commutative rings, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, and assume that $R$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $f:C	o R$ be a ring homomorphism, $s\ge0$, and $b_1,\ldots,b_s\in I$. Set $J=(b_1,\ldots,b_s)$ and assume that the composite $C\xrightarrow{f}R	o R/J$ is surjective. Let $E:C[[y_1,\ldots,y_s]]	o R$ be a ring homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] satisfying, for every $F=\sum_
u a_
u y^
u$ and $N\ge1$,
$$E(F)\equiv\sum_{|
u|<N}f(a_
u)b^
u\pmod{I^N},\qquad |
u|=\sum_j
u_j,\quad b^
u=\prod_jb_j^{
u_j}.$$
For every $z\in R$ there exist polynomials $H_N\in C[y_1,\ldots,y_s]$ for $N\ge0$, all of whose nonzero monomials have total degree $N$, and a series $S\in C[[y_1,\ldots,y_s]]$ such that, writing $S_N=\sum_{k<N}H_k$, one has
$$S_0=0,\qquad z-E(S_N)\in J^N,\qquad S_{N+1}-S_N=H_N\quad(N\ge0),$$
$$S_{<N}=S_N,\qquad E(S)-E(S_N)\in I^N\quad(N\ge1),\qquad E(S)=z.$$
Here polynomials are regarded as series when applying $E$, and $S_{<N}$ denotes the finite sum of the monomials of $S$ of total degree less than $N$. In particular $E$ is surjective. Zero polynomials are allowed; when $s=0$ one can take $H_N=0$ for every $N>0$.

proof.text:
First $J\subseteq I$ since every $b_j\in I$. For a polynomial $P=\sum_
u c_
u y^
u$ write $P(f,b)=\sum_
u f(c_
u)b^
u$. For any $M\ge1$, choose $L\ge M$ larger than every degree in the finite support of $P$. The assumed reduction formula gives $E(P)-P(f,b)\in I^L\subseteq I^M$. The separatedness in [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] makes this difference zero. This includes $P=0$ and constants. Thus evaluation of every polynomial is exactly its finite substitution, rather than merely congruent to it.

proof.text:
Fix $N\ge0$ and $r\in J^N$. The first clause of [lem-trf-finite-support-monomial-ideal-power], applied with its coefficient ring $A=R$, ideal $J=(b_1,\ldots,b_s)$ and exponent $k=N$, expresses $r$ as a finite sum of $R$-multiples of length-$N$ products of the $b_j$. Its irrelevant auxiliary data may be taken as $B=R$, $C=\mathrm{id}$, $P=\{0\}$ and $z^0=1$. Group the finite sum by exponent vector to obtain $r=\sum_{|
u|=N}r_
u b^
u$. For each nonzero coefficient choose $c_
u\in C$ with $r_
u-f(c_
u)\in J$, using the given surjection $C	o R/J$. Set $H=\sum c_
u y^
u$. Step 1 shows $r-E(H)=\sum(r_
u-f(c_
u))b^
u\in JJ^N=J^{N+1}$. This $H$ is homogeneous of degree $N$. For $N=0$ the sole monomial is $1$, so the same argument is precisely lifting $r mod J$.

proof.text: Choose such corrections recursively: start with $S_0=0$, for which $z-E(S_0)=z\in J^0=R$. Given $S_N$ with $r_N=z-E(S_N)\in J^N$, apply step 2 to $r_N$ to choose $H_N$ and put $S_{N+1}=S_N+H_N$. Additivity of the ring map $E$ gives $z-E(S_{N+1})=r_N-E(H_N)\in J^{N+1}$. Induction gives every required residual and increment identity and $S_N=\sum_{k<N}H_k$. Each sum is a polynomial of degree less than $N$.

source.place: Tag 09PZ (lemma-ci-well-defined), proof, third paragraph, omitted surjectivity details; explicit agent-supplied homogeneous approximation argument.

proof.text:
Using the coefficient-family definition [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], define the series $S$ by $[y^
u]S=[y^
u]H_{|
u|}$. For each $N$, the set of exponent vectors of total degree less than $N$ is finite: for $N>0$ each of its $s$ coordinates is less than $N$, and for $N=0$ the set is empty. Homogeneity means $[y^
u]H_k=0$ unless $|
u|=k$. Thus the coefficient of $y^
u$ in $\sum_{k<N}H_k$ equals that in $S$ when $|
u|<N$, and is zero otherwise. This proves $S_{<N}=S_N$ coefficient by coefficient, including $N=0$.

source.place: Tag 09PZ (lemma-ci-well-defined), proof, third paragraph, omitted surjectivity details; explicit agent-supplied homogeneous approximation argument.

proof.text: For $N\ge1$ apply the assumed reduction formula to $S$. By step 4 its finite substitution sum is $S_N(f,b)$, and by step 1 this equals $E(S_N)$. Consequently $E(S)-E(S_N)\in I^N$. Step 3 gives $z-E(S_N)\in J^N\subseteq I^N$, where the inclusion follows by multiplying $J\subseteq I$ repeatedly. Subtraction gives $z-E(S)\in I^N$ for every positive $N$. Separatedness [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] now yields $z=E(S)$. Since $z$ was arbitrary, $E$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 09PZ (lemma-ci-well-defined), proof, third paragraph, omitted surjectivity details; explicit agent-supplied homogeneous approximation argument.

proof.text: If $s=0$, the empty generated ideal $J$ is zero and the only exponent vector is the empty vector, of degree zero. The given surjection $C\to R/J=R$ supplies $H_0=c$ with $f(c)=z$, while for $N>0$ the residual is zero and one chooses $H_N=0$. Then $S=c$ and every preceding identity still holds. Zero corrections are allowed also for arbitrary $s$, so the argument covers $J=0$, nilpotent ideals, and the zero ring.

lean.statement: theorem exists_homogeneous_preimages_of_adic_evaluation {C : Type u} {R : Type v} [CommRing C] [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) [IsAdicComplete I R] (f : C →+* R) (s : ℕ) (b : Fin s → R) (hb : ∀ j : Fin s, b j ∈ I) (hf : Function.Surjective ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range b))).comp f)) (E : MvPowerSeries (Fin s) C →+* R) (hE : ∀ (F : MvPowerSeries (Fin s) C) (N : ℕ), 1 ≤ N → E F - MvPolynomial.eval₂ f b (F.truncTotal N) ∈ I ^ N) : (∀ z : R, ∃ (H : ℕ → MvPolynomial (Fin s) C) (S : MvPowerSeries (Fin s) C), (∀ N : ℕ, (H N).IsHomogeneous N) ∧ (∑ k ∈ Finset.range 0, H k) = 0 ∧ (∀ N : ℕ, z - E (MvPolynomial.toMvPowerSeries (∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, H k)) ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range b)) ^ N) ∧ (∀ N : ℕ, (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), H k) - (∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, H k) = H N) ∧ (∀ N : ℕ, S.truncTotal N = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, H k) ∧ (∀ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N → E S - E (MvPolynomial.toMvPowerSeries (∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, H k)) ∈ I ^ N) ∧ E S = z ∧ (s = 0 → ∀ N : ℕ, 0 < N → H N = 0)) ∧ Function.Surjective E
